subject: Choosing bedroom colours and finishes
hook: Three samples on the bed. One wardrobe on the wall.
ig:
Three samples on the bed. One wardrobe on the wall. Here's how a finish choice typically goes from shortlist to fitted.

The shortlist: three finishes, say matt white, oak-effect and charcoal.
Living with them: morning light, lamp light, next to the carpet.
Handles: gold or black, tried on the favourite.
3D: the colour seen at full scale on the design.
Made to match: panels edged in matching ABS in the workshop.
Fitted: soft-close doors and drawers set and checked.

The step people most often want to skip is leaving the samples out for a day or two. It's also the step that most often changes their mind.

These frames are concept images showing the principle. For real SUPERIO bedrooms, take a look at our showcase. Save this, and see genuine work via the link in bio.
fb:
How do you go from a handful of colour samples to a fitted wardrobe you're happy with for years? Here's how it typically works with us.

Pick three finishes you like, leave them in the bedroom for a day or two so you see them in different light, try the handles on your favourite, then see it on the full 3D design. After that it's made and edged to match in our Hanley workshop and fitted by our own team.

These are concept images to show the steps. Genuine SUPERIO bedroom furniture is on our showcase.

on_asset: F1: The shortlist — Three finishes chosen from the range, for example matt white, oak-effect and charcoal, laid out in the bedroom. | F2: Living with them — Samples left in place to be seen in morning light, evening lamplight and next to the flooring. | F3: Handles decided — Antique gold or matt black tried on the favourite, because the handle changes the finish. | F4: Seen in 3D — The chosen finish shown on the full design, so the scale of the colour is clear before anything is made. | F5: Made to match — Panels cut and edged in matching ABS in our Hanley workshop. | F6: Fitted — Installed by our own team, soft-close doors and drawers set and checked. | Concept image
